subject: Cost sensitivity + prefetch/cache scenarios for BrightBasket (post-demo)
messages:
From: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@brightbasket.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: cost modeling + cache assumptions (BrightBasket)

Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the walkthrough on routing and the dedicated warm prefix idea. A few follow-ups from our side to help us qualify budget and next steps:

- Monthly baseline: ~120M tokens (mix of short Q&A and long-form summaries).
- Daily peaks: ~3.5–4.5M tokens during promo windows (spikes matter for latency, but cost is monthly blended).
- Target effective price: we need to understand scenarios that land us at or below ~$2,800 / 1M tokens effective (that’s the internal threshold for starting a pilot).

Ask: can you send a concise sensitivity table showing effective $/1M under these inputs: list unit price (hosted) you quoted during call, and hit rates for caching at 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%? Also: how should we think about prefix cache vs. session-level KV caching — what hit rates are realistic for a grocery-retailer conversational workload (lots of short SKU lookups + basket summaries)?

If you can include a quick CSV with the scenario math we can drop this into our FinOps model. Also: we’ll likely need a 30-day pilot with telemetry (per-route token breakdown) if numbers look reasonable.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Hunter
Head of Product Operations
BrightBasket
procurement@brightbasket.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@brightbasket.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost modeling + cache assumptions (BrightBasket)

Alex — great to connect earlier. Attached is a simple sensitivity model (cache_sensitivity_model.csv) and a short recap below. I kept assumptions conservative so you can see downside + upside.

Key assumptions we used for the table:
- List (hosted) unit price for the primary generation model: $3,600 / 1M tokens (this is the glassbox per-token rate we use for baseline quoting).
- Cache operational cost: we treated prefix KV cache as near-zero marginal cost for hosted (few cents / GB-month — negligible at the token level for your volumes). If you run Dedicated on your cloud we can include infra markup; we left that out here and can add in a Dedicated line.
- "Effective billed tokens" = total_tokens * (1 - hit_rate). We applied hit_rate to total token consumption (this is conservative; in practice prefix cache hits usually apply to only the first N tokens per session, so the effective hit-rate on billable tokens can be higher for short-session-heavy workloads).

Scenario table (effective $ / 1M tokens):
- 0% hit: $3,600 / 1M
- 20% hit: $2,880 / 1M  (3,600 * (1 - 0.20))
- 40% hit: $2,160 / 1M  (3,600 * (1 - 0.40))
- 60% hit: $1,440 / 1M  (3,600 * (1 - 0.60))

Prefix cache nuance (retailer workload):
- Observed behavior from similar customers: warm prefix hit rates vary widely by UX. For BrightBasket-like flows (frequent short lookups + repeated cart summaries) we estimate:
  - Cold sessions (first-time user flow): low prefix reuse (0–5% hits).
  - Returning sessions within same user/session: prefix reuse 20–50% on small fixed prompts (e.g., system+context templates).
  - SKU lookup reuse (if you normalize prompts and use consistent templates): another 10–20% uplift.
Combined conservative composite hit-rate: 25–35% in early piloting; with prompt normalization + caching policy tuning we’ve seen 45–65% on similar retail pilots.

Quick worked example using your 120M tokens / month baseline:
- At 25% hit: billed tokens = 90M → cost = 90 * $3.6K = $324K → effective = $2,700 / 1M (meets your $2.8K threshold).
- At 35% hit: billed tokens = 78M → cost = 78 * $3.6K = $280.8K → effective ≈ $2,340 / 1M.

Attachments: cache_sensitivity_model.csv (simple rows for hit % vs billed tokens vs cost), and a one-page MAP draft (RB-MAP-draft.pdf) that outlines pilot metrics + telemetry we’d instrument.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We (Redwood) run a 30-day pilot with a low-friction integration (API keys + routing).
2) Measure observed prefix hit-rate across a 10K-sample of sessions and compute actual effective $/1M.
3) Based on the pilot data we’ll propose a committed disk for warm cache (if you want us to host it) or a Dedicated option with guaranteed hit-rate targets and a blended committed price.

Ben — adding you for pricing/discount notes.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com]

[Attachment: RB-MAP-draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost modeling + cache assumptions (BrightBasket)

Alex — thanks for the clarity. I pulled Evelyn's scenarios into our pricing sheet and ran a quick committed-offer sketch:

- If pilot shows >=30% sustained hit-rate we can offer a 10% committed discount off list (brings indicative list to $3,240 / 1M -> effective at 30% = $2,268 / 1M).
- If pilot gets to >=50% hit-rate we can move to a scaled committed price with a 20% discount (indicative list $2,880 / 1M -> effective at 50% = $1,440 / 1M).

Stephanie — can you confirm we can include a one-time onboarding credit for the 30-day pilot (we typically do $10–15K credit for integration work for deals at this scale)?

Alex — if that looks reasonable I’ll draft a simple MAP + PO template and we can get procurement looped in.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@brightbasket.com>

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick items from procurement side:

1) We’ll approve a 30-day pilot pending the MAP and a confirmation of the onboarding credit. Procurement needs the PO template and the pilot success criteria (observed >30% composite hit-rate and <5% 99th latency regression).
2) Please include the CSV math in the MAP so our FinOps team can validate the modeled effective $/1M before we sign.

If you can send the MAP + PO today we’ll aim to turn it in within 48 hours.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to running the sample.

Alex Hunter

BrightBasket
